answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted vouching that is slashable. Each new identity must lock a deposit, called a sparrow bond, before it can earn reputation. Vouchers stake part of their own bond on newcomers, and if a vouched agent is caught colluding, both lose stake. A crystal ledger records every vouch, and clusters sharing one funding source get one pooled vote, like a single knoll. Faking 100 identities therefore costs 100 bonds, with the whole cluster's stake at risk, while gaining only one vote.
